examples.ko: 오랜만이에요. 그사이 정말 많이 달라졌네요.
examples.en: It's been a while. You've really changed a lot in the meantime.

examples.ko: 바쁜 그사이에도 가족 생각을 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in that busy time, I never stopped thinking of my family.

examples.ko: 일이 끝나고 저녁 먹기 전 그사이가 제일 편해요.
examples.en: The gap between finishing work and eating dinner is the most relaxing.

explain: '그동안'은 쭉 이어진 기간을 말하고, '그사이'는 두 일 사이의 틈을 가리켜요. 그래서 '잠깐 자리를 비운 그사이'처럼 짧은 틈에 일어난 일을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '그 사이'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: It snowed in the meantime while I was sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띄어 쓴 모양이고, '에'를 붙여 그 틈에 일어난 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form; adding 에 points to something that happened in that gap.

phrases.en: It's been a while. You've grown a lot in the meantime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 만났을 때 변화를 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to note a change after a long time apart.
phrases.en_equiv: grew a lot in the meantime

phrases.en: An urgent matter came up in the meantime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 틈에 갑자기 일이 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something comes up suddenly in a short gap.
phrases.en_equiv: something came up in the meantime

explain_en: Neutral, the gap between two events — both speech and writing. '그동안' refers to a continuous period, while '그사이' points to the gap between two events. So it suits things that happen in a short gap, as in '잠깐 자리를 비운 그사이' (while I stepped away for a moment). You will also see it written as '그 사이'.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 맨날 게임만 해요.
examples.en: My younger brother does nothing but play games every day.

examples.ko: 맨날 늦는 친구 때문에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry at a friend who is late all the time.

examples.ko: 요즘 맨날 비가 와서 빨래가 안 말라요.
examples.en: It rains every day lately, so the laundry won't dry.

examples.ko: 맨날 라면만 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Eating only ramen every day isn't good for your health.

examples.ko: 우리는 어릴 때 맨날 같이 놀았어요.
examples.en: We played together every day when we were little.

examples.ko: 퇴근하고 맨날 집에서 드라마를 봐요.
examples.en: After work I watch dramas at home every day.

explain: '매일'과 비슷하지만 '똑같은 일이 계속 반복돼서 지겹다'는 느낌이 섞여 불평할 때 많이 써요. 뉴스·발표·글에서는 '매일'이나 '늘'을 쓰고, 말할 때 '맨날'이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I drink coffee every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맨날'과 뜻은 같지만 불평하는 느낌이 없고 글과 발표에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '맨날' but neutral, and fine in writing and presentations.

phrases.en: That friend is always smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맨날'보다 부드럽고 글에서도 자연스러운 '언제나'의 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer word for 'always' that also works in writing.

phrases.example: 저는 날마다 저녁에 동네를 한 바퀴 걸어요.
phrases.en: I walk around my neighborhood every evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맨날'과 뜻이 비슷하지만 불평하는 느낌이 없고 조금 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '맨날' but without the complaining tone, and a bit softer.

explain_en: Casual spoken — every day, often exaggerated for 'all the time'. Close to '매일' but it often carries a 'the same thing again and again, how tiresome' feel, so it is common in complaints. In news, presentations and writing use '매일' or '늘'; in speech '맨날' is more common.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 봄날에는 가족과 공원에서 산책해요.
examples.en: On warm spring days I take a walk in the park with my family.

examples.ko: 어느 봄날 아침에 그 친구를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met that friend one spring morning.

examples.ko: 봄날의 햇살이 창문으로 부드럽게 들어와요.
examples.en: The soft spring sunlight comes in through the window.

examples.ko: 저는 꽃이 피는 봄날이 제일 좋아요.
examples.en: I like spring days when flowers bloom best.

examples.ko: 봄날처럼 따뜻한 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a warm person like a spring day.

explain: '봄'은 계절 전체이고 봄날은 봄 중의 하루나 봄 같은 날씨를 말해요. 노래나 시에 자주 나와서 좋았던 시절을 '화양연화'나 '봄날'로 비유하기도 해요. 겨울에도 따뜻하면 '봄날 같다'고 말해요.

phrases.en: I went on a picnic with a friend on a warm spring day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 좋은 봄의 하루를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a nice day in spring.

phrases.en: It's winter, but today feels like a spring day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄이 아닐 때도 따뜻하면 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when it's warm even outside of spring.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel like a spring day

phrases.en: On spring mornings I can hear the birds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄 중의 어느 아침을 그림처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paints a picture of a morning in spring.

explain_en: 봄 is the whole season, while 봄날 is a single day in spring or a springlike day. It often appears in songs and poems, and 봄날 can also stand for the good days of one's life. A warm winter day can be called 봄날 같다.

examples.ko: 저는 오래전에 이 동네를 떠났어요.
examples.en: I left this neighborhood a long time ago.

examples.ko: 한국에서는 집에 들어갈 때 신발을 벗는 풍습이 오래전부터 있었어요.
examples.en: In Korea, the custom of taking off shoes when entering a home has existed since long ago.

examples.ko: 너무 오래전이라 이름이 기억나지 않아요.
examples.en: It was so long ago that I can't remember the name.

examples.ko: 오래전에 읽은 소설을 다시 읽었어요.
examples.en: I reread a novel I had read long ago.

explain: 한 단어이므로 '오래전'처럼 붙여 쓰고, 조사는 '오래전에, 오래전부터, 오래전의'로 이어져요. '옛날'은 훨씬 먼 과거나 이야기 속 시대에 어울리고, '오래전'은 몇 년이나 몇십 년 전처럼 내가 아는 과거에 써요. 반대로 가까운 과거는 '얼마 전', '최근'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This shop has been here for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그때부터 지금까지 이어지는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something continuing from long ago until now.

phrases.example: 아주 오래전 일이라 잘 기억이 안 나요.
phrases.en: It was so long ago that I don't remember well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아주'를 붙여 시간이 정말 오래됐다는 걸 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Aju' stresses that it was really a long time ago.

phrases.en: That is something from a long time ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 일을 설명하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when explaining that something is in the past.

explain_en: A long time ago, past point in time (오래전에) It is written as one word, '오래전', and takes particles as in '오래전에', '오래전부터' and '오래전의'. '옛날' suits a much farther past or storybook times, while '오래전' fits a past you personally know, such as years or decades ago. The recent past is '얼마 전' or '최근'.

examples.ko: 회사에 들어간 첫해에는 실수가 많았어요.
examples.en: In my first year at the company, I made a lot of mistakes.

examples.ko: 결혼 첫해에 우리는 작은 집에서 살았어요.
examples.en: In our first year of marriage, we lived in a small house.

examples.ko: 가게를 열고 첫해에 손님이 많지 않았어요.
examples.en: In the first year after opening the shop, there weren't many customers.

explain: '첫해'는 한 단어라서 붙여 써요. 그다음 해는 '이듬해'나 '둘째 해'라고 해요. '첫날, 첫눈, 첫사랑'처럼 '첫-'이 붙은 말이 많아요.

phrases.en: I studied hard from the first year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부터'를 붙여 첫해에 시작해서 계속된 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 부터 says something started in the first year and continued.

phrases.example: 결혼 첫해에 이사를 두 번 했어요.
phrases.en: In the first year of our marriage, we moved twice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 시작된 첫해를 말할 때 앞에 그 일을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the event before it to mean the first year of that event.

phrases.en: In the first year, everything felt unfamiliar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에는'을 붙여 첫해에 어땠는지 다른 해와 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에는 describes what the first year was like, often in contrast with later years.

explain_en: First year of a job or activity; plain, neutral (회사에 들어온 첫해) 첫해 is one word, written without a space. The year after it is 이듬해 or 둘째 해. Many words start with 첫-, such as 첫날, 첫눈 and 첫사랑.

en: first day of school; start of a new term

examples.ko: 방학이 끝나고 개학하면 많이 바빠져요.
examples.en: When vacation ends and school starts, I get very busy.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 삼월 이 일에 개학해요.
examples.en: Our school starts the term on March 2.

explain: 방학과 짝이 되는 말이라 '방학이 끝나고 개학했어요'처럼 같이 써요. 한국 학교는 3월에 새 학년이 시작돼서 '삼월 개학'은 특별한 날이에요.

phrases.en: School starts tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개학'을 동사로 바꾼 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 'gaehak'.

phrases.en: The principal spoke at the start-of-term ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 학기를 시작하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ceremony that begins a new term.

phrases.example: 개학이 얼마 안 남아서 숙제를 서둘러요.
phrases.en: School starts soon, so I am hurrying with my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개학이 곧 올 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when school is about to start.

explain_en: Start of a new term in primary and secondary schools. It pairs with 방학, as in '방학이 끝나고 개학했어요'. Korean schools start a new school year in March, so the March 개학 is a special day.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 학교 기숙사에서 생활해요.
examples.en: I'm living in the school dormitory now.

examples.ko: 외국에서 혼자 생활하는 건 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Living alone abroad isn't easy.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 건강하게 생활하려고 노력해요.
examples.en: I try to live healthily every day.

explain: '살다'는 사는 곳, '지내다'는 어떻게 보내는지를 가리키고, '생활하다'는 기숙사, 군대, 병원처럼 규칙이 있는 곳에서 지내는 모습에 어울려요. 말할 때는 '한국에서 살아요', '잘 지내요'가 더 자연스러워요. 명사 '생활'은 '학교 생활', '한국 생활'처럼 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I live in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '생활해요'보다 '살아요'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, 살아요 sounds more natural than 생활해요.

phrases.en: I am doing well in Korea these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떻게 보내는지를 말할 때 써요. 안부 인사에도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes how you are getting by; also common in greetings.

phrases.en: This neighborhood is convenient to live in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 편하다'를 붙여서 지내기 좋다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -기 편하다 says it is comfortable to live in.

explain_en: Emphasizes day-to-day living, routine and lifestyle in a place. '살다' is about where you live and '지내다' about how you spend your days; '생활하다' suits places with rules, such as dorms, the military, or a hospital. In speech '한국에서 살아요' and '잘 지내요' are more natural. The noun '생활' is more common, as in '학교 생활' and '한국 생활'.

gh: to live, reside; most common verb

p.n: 살다 only says where you live.

examples.ko: 엄마가 쌀가게에서 쌀 이십 킬로그램을 사 오셨어요.
examples.en: Mom bought twenty kilograms of rice at the rice shop.

examples.ko: 동네 쌀가게 아저씨가 집까지 배달해 주세요.
examples.en: The man at the neighborhood rice shop delivers to our house.

examples.ko: 이 쌀가게는 쌀 종류가 정말 다양해요.
examples.en: This rice shop has a really wide variety of rice.

examples.ko: 쌀가게에 햅쌀이 나왔는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked at the rice shop whether the new-harvest rice had come in.

examples.ko: 요즘은 쌀가게보다 인터넷으로 쌀을 많이 사요.
examples.en: These days people buy rice online more than at rice shops.

examples.ko: 시장 입구에 있던 쌀가게가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The rice shop at the market entrance has closed down.

explain: '쌀집'이라고도 해요. 요즘은 마트나 인터넷에서 쌀을 사는 사람이 많아서 동네 쌀가게는 예전보다 적어요. '쌀을 팔다·사다·배달하다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I bought rice at the neighborhood rice shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌀가게'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'ssalgage', and more common in speech.

phrases.en: I bought rice from the rice store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 쌀을 살 때 쓰는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A basic expression for buying rice at the store.
phrases.en_equiv: to buy rice at the rice store

phrases.en: The man from the rice store delivered the rice to us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 주인을 가깝게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to refer to the shop owner.
phrases.en_equiv: the man from the rice store

explain_en: It is also called '쌀집'. These days many people buy rice at supermarkets or online, so neighborhood rice shops are less common than before. It goes with '쌀을 팔다/사다/배달하다' (sell/buy/deliver rice).

t90.ax: This rice shop has a really wide variety of rice.

examples.ko: 저는 올해 대학교 졸업반이에요.
examples.en: I'm a senior in college this year.

examples.ko: 졸업반이 되니까 취업 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: Now that I'm a senior, I worry a lot about finding a job.

examples.ko: 졸업반 선배들이 후배들에게 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: The graduating seniors bought a meal for the juniors.

examples.ko: 우리 졸업반은 모두 서른 명이에요.
examples.en: Our graduating class has thirty students in total.

examples.ko: 졸업반이라서 요즘 졸업 작품 준비로 바빠요.
examples.en: I'm a senior, so I'm busy preparing my graduation project.

explain: 졸업을 앞둔 마지막 학년이나 그 학생들을 말해요. 대학교에서는 '4학년'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요. '졸업반이 되다', '졸업반 학생'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The graduating students are busy these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마지막 학년에 있는 학생들을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to students in their final year.

phrases.en: I will be a senior next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마지막 학년에 올라갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when moving up to the final year.

phrases.en: Since I'm a senior, I'm preparing to get a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 '-라서'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-라서' to give a reason.

explain_en: It refers to the final year before graduation or the students in it. In university it can be used much like '4학년' (fourth-year). Say '졸업반이 되다' (become a senior) or '졸업반 학생' (a senior student).
